successors.name: Duchy of Savoy
successors.text: the Duchy of Savoy restored by the Peace of Cateau-Cambresis in 1559

ledger.x: 1003: Humbert the White-Handed is made Count of Savoy.
1046: Otto marries into the March of Turin.
Aosta joins Savoy.
1218: the counts of Savoy succeed the Zähringen in Vaud.
1272: Bresse comes to Savoy.
ledger.cp: Bresse (previous lords not named on the page)

ledger.x: 1295: Chambéry becomes the capital.
1353: the war for Faucigny and Gex.
1355: the Treaty of Paris.
1355: Savoy is recognised in Faucigny and Gex.
1355: Savoy gives up its lands in Dauphiné.
28 September 1388: Nice and the Ubaye valley.
Piedmont cells appear in Cliopatria's 1395 shape (Turin province 13, Cuneo 5, Biella 4, Vercelli 2, Novara 1).
1401: Savoy buys the County of Geneva.
Cliopatria's 1402 shape adds 12 cells (Isère 4, Vercelli 2, Savoie 2, Haute-Savoie 2, Turin 1, Biella 1) that none of the pages opened explains.
1416: Savoy becomes a duchy.
Cliopatria's shape loses one cell on the south shore of Lake Neuchâtel in 1475.
1536: Bern annexes Vaud.
1536: France occupies the duchy.
1559: the occupation ends.
1559: the occupied duchy is restored and passes to the House of Savoy dossier.

wars.name: Savoyard war for Faucigny and Gex
wars.outcome: Savoy took Gex in the siege of 26 October to 11 November 1353 and was 'recognised as the undisputed sovereign of Faucigny and the county of Gex' by the Treaty of Paris of 1355, giving up its lands in Dauphiné beyond the Rhone and Guiers.

wars.name: Savoyard sieges of Geneva
wars.outcome: 'Charles launched a surprise attack in July 1534, but his army was beaten back'; 'A second siege in October 1535 was attempted, and again Charles's army was defeated.'

wars.name: Bernese annexation of Vaud
wars.outcome: 'By 1536 Bern had completely annexed the area.'

wars.name: Italian War of 1536-1538
wars.outcome: France invaded the duchy in 1536 ('Francis ordered the occupation of the duchy'); the Truce of Nice of 18 June 1538 'ended the war, leaving Turin in French hands'; the occupation lasted to 1559.

certainty.note: The lordships of the Alps and the Rhône are approximate; Savoy's limits moved with marriages and sales, not surveyed lines.
The Treaty of Paris of 1355 settled the Dauphiné frontier on 'the rivers Rhone and Guiers'; the county of Nice lay 'between the Mediterranean Sea, Var River and the southernmost crest of the Alps'.
The lands under French occupation and the exiled duke's remnant are known only as 'most of his lands'.
